trickyParts: events.Horizon: an observation is safe only once a LATER snapshot's xmin is above the observer's own xid; one snapshot cannot prove its own max(id) (xmax hole). Await waits for an observation that started after the call.

Relay: one mutex is held across each page's publish and the cursor move, and across subscribe and the cursor read, so streamEvents can hand over at the published cursor P with no gap and no repeat; sentDuringCatchup is gone.

Relay and hub cursors stay on the last existing row at or below H, so the existing reset check (row at the cursor gone or another created_at) still works; a detected reset calls Horizon.Reset and re-awaits.

The horizon observes on store.Pool.Horizon (2 connections): on the shared pool the relay queued behind ~1,500 requests per observation under load. A gap re-read asks only the horizon (no reset check), so a gap held open by a long transaction costs the shared pool nothing.
deviations: The plan's 1x pass thresholds (committed/offered >= 0.99, SSE p99 <= 1 s) are not met (0.72 and 86 s from creation) on INFRA-589's committed harness: once the lock is gone, the shared pool and the 2 CPUs saturate at 1x (INFRA-592, INFRA-512). INFRA-514's architect accepted this on 2026-10-27; it is recorded in the PR body.

Beyond the plan: store.Pool.Horizon, a 2-connection pool for the horizon's observations, and gap re-reads that skip the reset check. Overlaps INFRA-592's planned Live() pool; the architect agreed whichever merges second folds it in (comment on INFRA-592).
LockOwners skips ownerless events (no row to lock), so the xid is taken once, in Append.

Live SSE frames are slower after the change: 1x p50 after write response 21.2 s -> 49.1 s, 0.5x 0 -> 225 ms. Cause: the horizon waits for every write transaction holding an xid when an event's id was handed out, and write transactions hold xids for seconds during document work. INFRA-514's architect accepted it for this PR (option a); dispatch://INFRA-636 moves document work and write advice out of write transactions and must bring 0.5x back to no slower than before.
